question: What defines an adverse event in healthcare?

options.A: An intentional delay in administering medication
options.B: A natural progression of a terminal disease
options.C: An unintended injury resulting from clinical care
options.D: A normal side effect expected from treatment

explanation: Adverse events refer specifically to unintended harm caused by management or care rather than the natural course of the underlying illness. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h1)

question: Why do most healthcare errors occur according to modern patient safety frameworks?
explanation: Modern safety science demonstrates that errors usually arise from systemic vulnerabilities rather than isolated human failure. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h1)

question: What is the very first priority when an adverse event occurs?
explanation: Preserving human life and preventing worsening injury always supersedes administrative paperwork immediately after an event. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h2)

question: A patient receives the wrong intravenous drug and shows signs of distress. What action comes first?

options.A: Ask the ward manager for advice on reporting
options.B: Stop the infusion immediately and check vital signs
options.C: Document the medication error in the main chart
options.D: Leave the bedside to locate the prescribing doctor

explanation: Halting the harmful agent and assessing baseline vital signs stops ongoing injury before administrative tasks begin. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h2)

question: How should an adverse event be described in the official patient record?

options.A: Omitting the event to protect the hospital's name
options.B: Speculating on which staff member made the mistake
options.C: Using objective, factual, and descriptive language
options.D: Using emotional terms to express deep regret

explanation: Medical records require clear, unbiased descriptions of clinical findings and interventions without emotional or speculative commentary. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of an internal incident report separate from the patient chart?

options.A: To advertise hospital mistakes to the public health ministry
options.B: To drive quality improvement and track facility safety trends
options.C: To calculate monthly salary deductions for staff errors
options.D: To provide evidence for prosecuting negligent nurses in court

explanation: Internal reporting tools gather data anonymously or confidentially to identify system flaws and prevent future occurrences. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of a root cause analysis?

options.A: To find a specific staff member to punish publicly
options.B: To prove that the hospital bears no legal liability
options.C: To uncover underlying systemic factors behind an error
options.D: To rewrite every nursing textbook used in training

explanation: Root cause analysis looks deep into workflows, equipment, and environment rather than stopping at human blame. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h4)

question: Why do investigators repeatedly ask 'why' during an adverse event review?

options.A: To find evidence of deliberate criminal intent
options.B: To move past surface human error to systemic causes
options.C: To prolong the investigation until public attention fades
options.D: To confuse the nursing staff during formal interviews

explanation: Iterative questioning peels back layers of operational complexity to reveal the true operational breakdowns. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h4)

question: What core principle should guide communication with families after an adverse event?

options.A: Complete silence until a lawyer arrives on site
options.B: Honest and transparent disclosure of known facts
options.C: Minimizing the severity of the injury to avoid panic
options.D: Shifting the blame entirely to junior student nurses

explanation: Patients and families deserve truthful explanations delivered with empathy and professional accountability following care mishaps. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h5)

question: A family expresses anger and grief after a preventable medication complication. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Walk away immediately to avoid difficult conversations
options.B: Tell them to stop complaining because mistakes happen
options.C: Listen with empathy and acknowledge their emotional pain
options.D: Promise that the responsible nurse will be jailed today

explanation: Validating patient and family emotions is an essential component of professional crisis management and compassionate care. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h5)

question: What is a key characteristic of a just culture in healthcare?

options.A: Ignoring minor errors to maintain staff morale on wards
options.B: Blaming the most junior team member for system failures
options.C: Punishing every single mistake with immediate termination
options.D: Encouraging error reporting without fear of unfair punishment

explanation: A just culture creates psychological safety so staff report near misses and errors openly for institutional learning. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h6)

question: How does a just culture evaluate human involvement in an adverse event?

options.A: By distinguishing human error from reckless behavior
options.B: By assuming all staff members act with malicious intent
options.C: By ignoring individual actions and blaming only the government
options.D: By treating all clinical mistakes with the exact same penalty

explanation: Just culture frameworks assess behavioral choices to apply appropriate coaching, system redesign, or disciplinary action. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h6)

question: What is the final essential step after investigating an adverse event?

options.A: Reducing staff shift hours to minimize fatigue risks
options.B: Implementing corrective actions and system improvements
options.C: Issuing a public warning against the affected patient
options.D: Filing away the paperwork and returning to normal routines

explanation: Investigations must culminate in actionable system changes that prevent the same error from happening again. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h7)

question: Why must quality assurance teams monitor new safety interventions after implementation?

options.A: To comply with local tax regulations for medical facilities
options.B: To verify that the changes actually reduce recurrence risks
options.C: To find new reasons to discipline underperforming nurses
options.D: To justify increasing patient admission fees across the ward

explanation: Monitoring ensures that newly introduced protocols or equipment modifications successfully resolve the original safety vulnerability. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h7)
